'''Dror Bar-Natan''' ({{langx|he|דרוֹר בָר-נָתָן}}; born January 30, 1966) is a Canadian-Israeli [[mathematician]] specializing in [[knot theory]], [[finite type invariant]]s, and [[Khovanov homology]]. He is currently a professor at the [[University of Toronto Department of Mathematics|University of Toronto]].

==Education==
Bar-Natan earned his [[B.Sc.|BSc]] in mathematics at [[Tel Aviv University]] in 1984.  After performing his [[Conscription in Israel|mandatory military service]] as a teacher, he went to study at [[Princeton University]] in 1987. He obtained his [[Ph.D.|PhD]] in mathematics from Princeton in 1991, under the direction of [[physicist]] [[Edward Witten]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Dror Bar-Natan |url=http://genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=31292 |website=[[Mathematics Genealogy Project]] |access-date=20 December 2010}}</ref>

==Professorship==
After holding a [[Benjamin Peirce]] Assistant Professorship at [[Harvard University]] for four years from 1991 to 1995, he returned to Israel, and became associate professor at the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]].  He moved to the [[University of Toronto]] in 2002, and was promoted to full professor in 2006.<ref name="math.toronto.edu">[http://www.math.toronto.edu/~drorbn/CV/CV.html Dror Bar-Natan — Curriculum Vitae]</ref>

==Personal life==
Bar-Natan holds US, Israeli, and Canadian citizenship, and currently resides in Canada. Bar-Natan originally refused to take the [[Oath of Citizenship (Canada)|Canadian citizenship oath]] because it would require him to swear allegiance to royalty.<ref>{{cite news|last=Perkel|first=Colin|title=Canadian citizenship oath to Queen will be challenged in court|url=https://www.thestar.com/news/canada/2013/07/11/canadian_citizenship_oath_to_queen_will_be_challenged_in_court.html|accessdate=8 April 2014|newspaper=[[Toronto Star]]|date=12 July 2013}}</ref> He later decided to become a citizen but publicly announced his intention to renounce the oath immediately after becoming a citizen,<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/toronto/oath-allegiance-queen-dror-1.3343188|accessdate=23 August 2026|newspaper=[[CBC News]]|date=30 November 2015|title=New Canadian to renounce oath of allegiance to Queen Elizabeth|last=Mehta|first=Diana}}</ref> which he did so in front of the presiding judge at his citizenship ceremony on November 30, 2015.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Barber |first1=John |title=Canadian republic advocates hope new government has less 'loyalty to royalty' |url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2015/dec/03/canada-republicans-trudeau-queen-elizabeth |access-date=27 June 2021 |newspaper=[[The Guardian]] |date=3 December 2015}}</ref>

From his former marriage to mathematician [[Yael Karshon]] he has two sons, Assaf and Itai.<ref name="math.toronto.edu"/>

==Research==
In 1999, Bar-Natan collaborated on a paper with the goal of mathematically refuting claims made in ''[[The Bible Code (book)|The Bible Code]]'' by [[Michael Drosnin]] that hidden messages could be deciphered from within the [[Bible]]. In particular, the paper demonstrated that practically any "code" could be found within the Bible, thereby debunking Drosnin's "discovery" of specific codes. This work is outside the main scope of his academic interests, although he is known for it because of the popularity of ''[[The Bible Code (book)|The Bible Code]]''.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=McKay |first1=Brendan |last2=Bar-Natan |first2=Dror |last3=Bar-Hillel |first3=Maya |last4=Kalai |first4=Gil |jstor=2676736 |journal=[[Statistical Science]] |volume=14 |issue=2 |year=1999 |pages=150-173 |title=Solving the Bible Code puzzle |author1-link=Brendan McKay (mathematician) |author3-link=Maya Bar-Hillel |author4-link=Gil Kalai}}</ref>

Academically, Bar-Natan has made significant contributions to the formalization of [[Khovanov homology]].

Bar-Natan was a member of the Editorial Board for the journal ''[[Compositio Mathematica]]'' for 10 years, until 2010.<ref name="math.toronto.edu" />
